title: Definition of 'consumer'
summary: Defines who counts as a consumer: a person who buys goods or hires or avails of services for consideration, other than for resale or a commercial purpose.

title: Definition of 'defect'
summary: Defines a defect in goods: any fault or imperfection in quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard required by law or claimed by the seller.

title: Definition of 'deficiency'
summary: Defines deficiency in service: any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature or manner of performance required by law or contract.

title: Definition of 'unfair trade practice'
summary: Defines unfair trade practices, including false or misleading representations about goods or services and refusing to take back or refund defective goods within the stated period.

title: Manner of filing a complaint
summary: Provides how a consumer may file a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

title: Findings and reliefs of the District Commission
summary: Lists the reliefs a District Commission may order when a complaint is proved, including removal of defects, replacement, refund of the price, compensation and costs.

title: Limitation period
summary: Provides the period within which a consumer complaint must be filed, with power to condone delay for sufficient cause.

title: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds
summary: Makes dishonour of a cheque for insufficiency of funds or exceeding the arrangement an offence, subject to presentation within validity, a written demand within the statutory period, and non-payment after the notice period.

title: Presumption in favour of the holder
summary: Presumes, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received it for the discharge, in whole or in part, of a debt or liability.

title: Cognizance of offences
summary: Governs who may complain and the time within which a complaint must be made after the cause of action arises.

title: Summary trial
summary: Provides for summary trial of these offences and empowers the court to order compensation and interest.

title: What agreements are contracts
summary: States the essentials of a valid contract: free consent of competent parties, lawful consideration and a lawful object, not expressly declared void.

title: Obligation of parties to contracts
summary: Requires parties to perform, or offer to perform, their promises unless performance is dispensed with or excused by law.

title: Compensation for loss caused by breach of contract
summary: Entitles the party who suffers a breach to compensation for loss that naturally arose in the usual course of things or that both parties knew likely to result, but not for remote or indirect loss.

title: Compensation where a sum is named as a penalty
summary: Allows reasonable compensation, not exceeding the amount named, where a contract fixes a sum payable on breach.

title: Bar of limitation
summary: Provides that a suit instituted after the prescribed period is to be dismissed even if limitation is not set up as a defence.

title: Effect of acknowledgment in writing
summary: Provides that a written acknowledgment of liability signed before the period expires gives a fresh period of limitation.

title: Interest in proceedings for recovery of debt
summary: Allows the court to award interest on a debt or damages for the period before the proceedings, at a rate it considers reasonable.

title: Interest on decree
summary: Allows the court to order interest on the principal sum from the date of the suit to the date of the decree and from decree to payment.

title: Implied conditions as to quality or fitness
summary: Sets out when goods sold must be fit for the buyer's purpose or of merchantable quality, even though there is no express term.

title: Obligation after an agreement is found void
summary: Requires a person who has received an advantage under an agreement that is discovered to be void, or a contract that becomes void, to restore it or make compensation.
